subtitle: Channel Vocoder
tagline: Stamps the spectral movement of a voice or rhythm onto a built-in synth or an external carrier, with 8 to 64 bands and five synthesis types.

body.lead: TB Vocoder is a real-time channel vocoder. It analyses the source in a bank of frequency bands and imprints the movement of each band onto a carrier, so the rhythm and articulation of the source stay recognisable while the tone becomes synthetic.

body.p: In SELF mode no second track is needed: the built-in synth is the carrier, so you can load TB Vocoder on a vocal or rhythmic source and start immediately. You can also feed an external carrier through the sidechain input. Choose 8 to 64 analysis bands, set the active frequency range, tune and colour the synth, and shape the response, whitening, width, and sibilance.

ul: Filterbank of 8 to 64 bands with an adjustable LOW and HIGH range
Built-in SELF synth with up to 100 detuned voices, tuning, and a saw-to-pulse COLOR
External carrier through the sidechain input, with automatic fallback to SELF
Five synthesis types: VOCODE, WHISPER, MORPH, RING, and INVERT
SIBILANCE lets consonants read through the synth
Four-band PRESSURE compression and a TONE tilt after cross-synthesis
Resynthesis spectrum display with SOURCE, CARRIER, and OUTPUT meters
119 factory presets in 12 banks, plus Init and user presets

note.title: About this manual
text: This manual describes TB Vocoder 2.0.0 for Windows (VST3), which is published as a beta. The current macOS build is version 1.0.3; it uses a different control set, including MIDI carrier input, and differs from the descriptions here.

ol: Insert TB Vocoder on a vocal or another rhythmic source. The internal synth is the carrier (`SIDECHAIN` shows SELF).
Play the track. Choose a preset {{1}}, or start from Init and set `BANDS` {{4}}: fewer bands sound retro, more bands are more intelligible.
Set the synth pitch with `TUNE` and its colour with `COLOR` {{3}}.
Shape the response with `ATTACK` and `RELEASE` {{4}}, and remove background noise with `FLOOR` {{5}}.
Blend with `MIX` and set the level with `OUTPUT` {{6}}.

rows: SELF uses the internal synth as the carrier. EXTERNAL uses the plug-in's Carrier (sidechain) input while enabled, and falls back to SELF when that input is unavailable.
Transposes the internal synth carrier in semitones; 0 st is the original pitch, A. No effect on an external carrier.
Morphs the internal synth from a full sawtooth to a narrowing pulse. No effect on an external carrier.
Number of detuned voices in the internal synth.
Width of the synthesis bands. Low is wide and blurred; high is narrow and singing.
Swaps the carrier for noise while the source is unvoiced, so consonants read through the synth.
Filterbank resolution. Few bands are coarse and retro; many bands track formants closely and stay intelligible.
Smears the analysis envelopes across neighbouring bands. Low is broad and soft; high keeps fine spectral detail.
Lowest band centre. Raise it to keep the bank off a bass-heavy source; lower it to imprint the low end as well.
Highest band centre. Above it, the source is not imprinted.
How fast each band envelope rises. Short is percussive and articulate; long softens consonant edges.
How fast each band envelope falls. Short is tight and gated; long smears words into each other.
VOCODE, WHISPER, MORPH, RING, INVERT · VOCODE
Synthesis method: classic band vocoding, a noise-carrier whisper, a spectral morph, per-band ring modulation, or an inverted imprint.
Morphs from a carrier gated by the source level to the full spectral imprint.
0% keeps the carrier's own spectral balance; 100% makes every output band match the source band exactly.
Stops low-level source noise from opening the spectral imprint.
Moves the spectral imprint without retuning the carrier.
Stretches or compresses the imprint around 1 kHz without pitch detection.
Four-band upward and downward compression after cross-synthesis.
Tilts the compressed result between weight and brightness.
Stereo spread of the processed signal only. 0% is mono, 100% is unchanged.
Blends the recorded source with the transformed synth.

ol: In your DAW, route the carrier track (for example a synth pad) to TB Vocoder's sidechain input.
Play both tracks. The CARRIER meter shows the carrier level. TUNE, COLOR, and COUNT have no effect on an external carrier.

body.p: Step through presets with the arrows, or open the list to choose a factory or user preset. Save stores the complete state as a .tbvocoderpreset file. The name shows CUSTOM after you change a setting. Undo and Redo step through recent changes.

The factory set has 119 presets in 12 banks: Essentials, Robots, Whispers, Morph & Formant, Ring & Metal, Invert & Hollow, Low & Chant, Rhythmic, Wide & Cloud, OTT & Squash, Vocoder Resynth, and Carrier Shapes. Examples include **Classic Talk Box**, **Robot Choir**, **Air Whisper**, **Crystal Formant**, **100 Voice Cloud**, **Final Boss Vocoder**, and the band-count series from **Vintage Eight** to **Surgical Sixty Four**.

warn.text: Presets saved before version 2.0 cannot be loaded, because they use a filterbank and TYPE list that no longer exist.

body.p: Starting points for common jobs. Adjust them by ear.

recipes.title: Classic robot voice
settings: Classic Talk Box or Robot Choir
steps: Set TUNE to the song key so the carrier sits in tune.
Raise SIBILANCE until consonants read clearly.

recipes.title: Retro low-band vocoder
steps: Fewer bands are less intelligible; keep the vocal part simple.

recipes.title: Rhythmic synth from drums

steps: Use a pad as an external carrier for chords.

recipes.title: Whisper texture
steps: Blend under the dry vocal for atmosphere.

Vocoder, Whisper, Morph, Ring Mod, Invert

Rebuilt the vocoder around a configurable multi-band filterbank with LOW and HIGH range, attack, release, width, and resynthesis controls. Redesigned the interface into four focused panels and introduced a new state format for the 23-control engine.
